question: As per Census 2011, which of the following streams of migration has the highest percentage?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rural to rural**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per Census 2011, the most common type of internal migration in India is from **rural areas to other rural areas**.
 
• This type of migration accounts for about **47.4%** of the total internal migration.
 
• One of the major reasons for rural to rural migration is **marriage**, especially among women.
 
• Another reason is the movement of **agricultural laborers** in search of work.
 
• Rural to rural migration is also driven by **seasonal work** in agriculture and related sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census 2011 Migration Data**

 
 
• The Census of India 2011 provides detailed data on migration patterns within the country.
 
• It categorizes migration into four streams: rural to rural, rural to urban, urban to urban, and urban to rural.
 
• Understanding these patterns helps in planning and policy formulation for regional development.
 
 
 
• **Types of Migration**
 
 
• **Internal Migration:** Movement within a country, such as from one state or region to another.
 
• **External Migration:** Movement across country boundaries, also known as international migration.
 
 
 
• **Reasons for Migration**
 
 
• **Economic:** Search for better employment opportunities and living conditions.
 
• **Social:** Marriage, family reunification, and education.
 
• **Environmental:** Natural disasters, climate change, and environmental degradation.
 
• **Political:** Conflict, persecution, and instability.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Migration**
 
 
• Can lead to **urbanization** and growth of cities.
 
• May cause **strain on urban infrastructure** and resources.
 
• Contributes to **cultural exchange** and diversity.
 
• Can result in **brain drain** or **skill shortages** in the areas of origin.
